children: is seeing slightly shorter global delivery times for its premium iPhone 18 models than it did at the same stage of last year's launch, according to Bank of America, offering an early but mixed read on demand. The data suggest iPhone 18 Pro demand remains broadly comparable with the iPhone 17 cycle, while unusually short waits in China and sizable price increases across several markets deserve closer attention from investors.

"Our tracking of iPhone ship dates on Apple's own website, and various carrier websites, indicates that as of Sep 21st (10 days after preorders started on Fri Sep 12th), ship time (in days) for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models are roughly similar to last year at this point in the preorder cycle," BofA analyst Wamsi Mohan said.
Globally, the iPhone 18 Pro currently carries an average 14-day wait, versus 15 days for the iPhone 17 Pro last year. The Pro Max stands at 20 days, compared with 21 days a year earlier.
"Lead time trends are incrementally positive, with iPhone 18 Pro ship dates stable at 14 days, compared to the iPhone 17 Pro, which saw a slight moderation from 18 days to 15 days," Mohan added.

China is the standout. Delivery times there are just 11 days for the Pro and 15 days for the Pro Max, below other major regions. BofA said some buyers may be waiting for Apple's iPhone Duo, complicating interpretation of the shorter lead times.
Pricing adds another variable. Pro-model prices increased 20% to 23% year over year in Japan and India, 8% to 12% in China, the U.K., Germany and the U.S., and roughly 5% in Australia.
For Apple investors, early ship times should be treated as a demand signal, not definitive proof of sales strength.
The key metrics now are actual sell-through, Pro and Pro Max mix, China demand and whether consumers absorb higher prices without hurting unit volumes.

Shorter Chinese lead times would become more concerning if they persist after the Duo launches. Conversely, stable premium-model demand despite substantial price increases could support revenue and margins.
BofA maintained its Buy rating and $370 price target, keeping the focus on whether Apple can convert broadly steady launch demand into stronger earnings growth.

title: Bank of America Flags Mixed iPhone 18 Demand Signal
